title: copilot --json update
description: Output of `copilot --json update` (cli-copilot foundation). Reports the outcome of syncing each resolved `component: cli` tier's read-only mirror (`config/sync.py`) plus a presence-only managed-secret-store readiness report (`config/store_readiness.py`). Computed entirely CLI-side -- a consumer (e.g. Control Tower) only ever renders this payload (invariant #1: parse, never compute); it contains no secret VALUE, ever. Sibling contract to `docs/schemas/layers.schema.json` (`copilot --json layers`), which reports resolved chain/service provenance without syncing anything.

schema_version.description: Contract version for this payload shape.

component.description: Which CSE component this report covers. Always 'cli' for this CLI's own `update` command.

overall.description: 'ok': every layer cloned/pulled cleanly (or there were zero layers). 'attention': at least one layer was 'held' (never-destroy gate) or 'skipped' (semver range with no matching tag) -- no data was lost, but something needs a human look. 'error': at least one layer's sync itself failed (network/git error).

layers.description: Per-layer sync outcome, in the same precedence order as `copilot --json layers`'s `chain` (highest precedence first). Empty when no `copilot.layers.yml` resolves a 'cli' component chain at all -- nothing to sync.

store.description: Presence-only managed-secret-store readiness report -- never a secret value, never the result of a network auth attempt, never triggers provisioning.

id.description: Stable layer identifier from the manifest, e.g. 'org-acme'.

ref.description: This layer's declared `source.ref`, exactly as written in the manifest -- may be a concrete branch/tag/SHA or a semver RANGE (e.g. '^1.4.5').

resolved_ref.description: The concrete ref actually used/considered for this sync. Equal to `ref` when `ref` was already concrete. The picked tag when `ref` was a semver range that resolved successfully (e.g. 'v1.5.9' for a `ref` of '^1.4.5'). Empty string when no ref could be resolved at all (malformed range, tag listing failed, or no tag satisfied the range) -- `action` is 'skipped' or 'error' in that case.

action.description: 'cloned': mirror was absent and is now cloned. 'pulled': mirror existed, was clean, and was fast-forwarded. 'held': the never-destroy gate withheld a write (dirty tree, unpushed local commits, unreadable status, or a non-git occupant at the mirror path) -- zero writes occurred. 'skipped': a semver-range `ref` had no tag satisfying it -- zero writes occurred. 'error': the sync itself failed (network/git error) -- zero writes assumed, never guaranteed beyond what git itself guarantees on a failed clone/pull.

detail.description: Human-readable one-line reason/summary for `action`, e.g. 'local changes', '@ v1.5.9 (^1.4.5)', 'no tag matches '^1.4.5''.

status.description: 'ready': a layer declares store config and either a complete GitHub-broker configuration or a present legacy Universal Auth pair. This presence-only update report does NOT claim live authentication succeeded; its detail says live broker access is checked when used. 'creds_missing': the selected authentication configuration is incomplete. 'none': no layer in the resolved chain declares store config at all.

detail.description: Human-readable status line, identical to what the non-JSON `update` output prints. Never contains a secret value.

layer_id.description: The nearest layer declaring the store, or null when `status` is 'none'.
